source_refs.note: Topic 2.6.3, printed pages 33-34: the d and f orbitals (Figure 2.7), with Quick Check 2.4 as the self-check.

blocks.text: In a given shell the d orbitals have different shapes and orientations in space. The dxy, dxz and dyz orbitals lie in the xy, xz and yz planes respectively. The lobes of the dx2-y2 orbital lie along the x and y axes. The dz2 orbital has two lobes along the z axis and a doughnut in the xy plane. These are the five d orbitals, for l = 2. An f subshell has seven orientations in space, that is seven f orbitals, but their shapes are very complicated.

blocks.alt: Five sets of axes with the five d orbitals. dxy, dyz and dxz each have four lobes lying between the axes of their plane; dx2-y2 has four lobes along the x and y axes; dz2 has two lobes along the z axis and a ring round the middle in the x-y plane. Darker and lighter lobes show opposite signs.
blocks.caption: The shapes of the five 3d orbitals (original diagram after Figure 2.7).
